View attachment 3559920
Click to expand...
It’s very close for me, but in my opinion I think it goes:

5. Uta - Helped Tsuneyo deal with her father’s situation because she endured something similar with her grandfather, and of course was there for Io during all her hardships.

4. Touka - She literally helped a random homeless person in the Old District for no other reason other than compassion. If that isn’t the textbook definition of kindness, I dunno what is. We also see this Touka’s kind (and maternal) nature on display when it comes to comforting Yasu, and more recently, Akira.

3. Futaba - She’s been a nice person throughout the majority of the game. Just look at the most recent update with Imani and calling her beautiful. Hits you right in the feels… Or all the shit she took from Yumi, and yet she was still the more mature person in the end and let bygones be bygones (damn you, Nodoka!). The only reason she isn’t ahead is if we’re basing this off of pure ‘kindness’ and selfless deeds, I feel only two others outrank her.

2. Noriko - Noriko is an angel. It’s true. You can’t deny it! Sorry, Maya.

Okay, so, we know she helps Akira in regaining his memories (see “Spotless Mind”) and she has a heavy role to play in his past, not to mention she loves him a lot, but what about beyond him? What makes Noriko so ‘kind’ exactly?

Let’s take Yumi’s recent event “Kid of the Month” for instance, after Noriko offers Yumi a job at the convenience store in the Old District. Despite Yumi’s protests and even occasional threats, Noriko shows nothing but kindness towards her, and even comforts her when the television triggers an uncomfortable memory from her past.

1. Karin - This isn’t even a surprise. I mean… Karin is the purest character in the game, bar none.

Want to know why Karin is at the top of the list? Besides the rest of the time she’s on screen, I mean.

Play the event “Touch of Grey”. She goes out of her way to appease literally everyone. She’s a perfect soul, and she didn’t deserve what happened to her at karaoke. Fuck you, Pareidolia.

Here’s hoping Kirin will learn to appreciate her sister a bit more in the near future, because she definitely does deserve it.

siegabro said:
I'm surprised there isn't Ayane in the original question - she always struck me as a very kind character, just a bit more developed. Meaning, she had encountered hostility more and learned to stand her ground (e.g. against Kirin), which may make her look less kind (but doesn't really).

Since there was Noriko in the question and since I forcefully injected Ayane here, here's smth I've been thinking about: am I the only one who thinks Noriko and Ayane basically have the same personality, just with different life situations?
1. Both are kind to a fault. Ayane deeply loves people around her and seeing them getting hurt really gets to her, like finding Ami stabbed in the last reset or Maya getting reset now. Her default attitude to all around her is exceptionally friendly and, unlike other friendly girls, there is not as much room for jealosy (Chika) or anger (Rin comes to mind). Her kindness hurts her as she cares about Sensei to the point of tolerating him cheating on her and accepts other girls being in love with him.
Meanwhile, Noriko being a martyr is explicitly stated in the story, and it is quite convincing, so I don't even feel like recounting arguments.
2. Both are brave. Ayane keeps positive attitude in the face of timeloops and apocalypse, stands up to Kirin, and does a million more little things, like driving away Yumi when she picks on Futaba in the shower, etc. Noriko never gave up on searching for Sensei and was brave enough to show him Niki's old letters when she felt it could endanger their relationship but was a right thing to do.
3. Both are cheerful and friendly. Ayane and Noriko light up the room and make friends with the most unlikely characters, like Ayane with Sana or Noriko with Yumi.
4. Both obsess about Sensei and are fake yanderes initially. These are more superficial qualities, but they work even better in terms of proving similarities. Ayane and Noriko are the only ones who openly proclaimed their undying love for Sensei as soon as they got the chance. And they both at the start of their storylines seemed the craziest and the most fixated on him. Heck, as stereotypical yanderes they are the only ones known for constantly carrying weapons (Noriko's knife and Ayane's various assortment of guns and swords).

I do feel like they're the same character, just with different quirks and places in the story. There are, of course, little things unique to each one of them, e.g. Ayane wanting to have a shit ton of kids and Noriko being an idealistic rebel with creative (musical) drive. But these are details, and I feel like the only real differences are circumstantial - their situations being different. Noriko's story seems to be about unreciprocated (yet) love, being a martyr and a constant second place, and her keeping her rightiousness and idealism in spite of this. Ayane, I feel, is more about loving in the face of adversity - blackmail, cheating, competition.

And I wouldn't say that there is something wrong with these two having the same basic characteristics - unique situations are enough for their stories to play out differently and in an entertaining way. I'm just trying to sort out my own confusion about this, as I feel like I enjoy Noriko the most out of all the characters, yet there is Ayane, who is nearly identical to her in most regards, but she is somehow a bit lower on my tierlist.
What do you people think?
Click to expand...
I think Ayane's kindness is more like a mask she wears.

The real Ayane wants Sensei all for herself, has tried to fuck him on the beds of her best friends, possibly stole Ami's first kiss to cover up her lies, and there was a Main Event that became a deleted scene called 'Horrible People' where she sucked Sensei off under his desk while Ami was talking about wanting to spend time with him, which more or less emphasized that Ayane kind of sucks in more ways than one:
Ayane - "We're horrible people, aren't we?"
(Probably too much, hence it becoming a deleted scene while Sel probably prefers it being more subtle.)

Ayane seems to be kind of a shitty person deep down, which may be implied by her causing trouble for businesses, manslaughtering Janitors, and lying to and/or using everyone who's there for her, like Ami and Sana. (Keep in mind Ami and Sana have likely been there for her since her mother left her at 11)

When it comes down to it, Ayane simply seems out for herself:
Ayane - "I'm the only one. I'm the only one. I'm the only one. I'm the only one. I'm the only one. I'm the only one. I'm the only one. I'm the only one. I'm the only one. I'm the only one. I'm the only one. I'm the only one."
And there's nothing we can do to stop her:
Paper Ayane - "I literally just told you that. There's nothing you can do to stop me."

Frankly, Ayane may have even played a part in Maya's crumbling based off how she was acting before it:
Ayane - "Unfortunately, I promised I wouldn't tell you. It's nothing but good news, though. For me, definitely. And...for all of us. I think. But that last part is more of an expectation than actually knowing."
And how Yasu implied she knew Ayane wanted to take Maya's place:
Yasu - "To take her place."
Which she kind of has, albeit probably not in the way she wanted.

Noriko on the other hand wishes Ayane luck in her pursuit of Sensei:
Ayane - "But I'm not ashamed to follow my heart. And I know that I have a better chance at ending up with Sensei than anyone."
Noriko - "And I wish you luck in that regard."
And basically wants everyone to be happy, whether it's Ami, Maya, or Uta:
Noriko - "Because in my master plan, we all live happily ever after together."
- "Maya, as much as you hate me, I care about you. And even if there's an earth-shattering rivalry between us, I don't actually want to hurt you. I want you to be happy."
- "I want you to be happy."

It's also been shown that Noriko is more perceptive than Ayane:
Noriko - "So you're not jealous of Otoha because Rin is crushing on her?"
Ayane - "How didn't I notice?"
- "Molly...I'm so sorry I didn't notice earlier. I wouldn't have even chased after you if I knew that's what it was."
Or at least more Empathetic.

Overall: Ayane and Noriko are similar in their outspoken love for Sensei, but are notably different in how they spend their time, think, and treat others.

I'm surprised there isn't Ayane in the original question - she always struck me as a very kind character, just a bit more developed. Meaning, she had encountered hostility more and learned to stand her ground (e.g. against Kirin), which may make her look less kind (but doesn't really).

Since there was Noriko in the question and since I forcefully injected Ayane here, here's smth I've been thinking about: am I the only one who thinks Noriko and Ayane basically have the same personality, just with different life situations?
1. Both are kind to a fault. Ayane deeply loves people around her and seeing them getting hurt really gets to her, like finding Ami stabbed in the last reset or Maya getting reset now. Her default attitude to all around her is exceptionally friendly and, unlike other friendly girls, there is not as much room for jealosy (Chika) or anger (Rin comes to mind). Her kindness hurts her as she cares about Sensei to the point of tolerating him cheating on her and accepts other girls being in love with him.
Meanwhile, Noriko being a martyr is explicitly stated in the story, and it is quite convincing, so I don't even feel like recounting arguments.
2. Both are brave. Ayane keeps positive attitude in the face of timeloops and apocalypse, stands up to Kirin, and does a million more little things, like driving away Yumi when she picks on Futaba in the shower, etc. Noriko never gave up on searching for Sensei and was brave enough to show him Niki's old letters when she felt it could endanger their relationship but was a right thing to do.
3. Both are cheerful and friendly. Ayane and Noriko light up the room and make friends with the most unlikely characters, like Ayane with Sana or Noriko with Yumi.
4. Both obsess about Sensei and are fake yanderes initially. These are more superficial qualities, but they work even better in terms of proving similarities. Ayane and Noriko are the only ones who openly proclaimed their undying love for Sensei as soon as they got the chance. And they both at the start of their storylines seemed the craziest and the most fixated on him. Heck, as stereotypical yanderes they are the only ones known for constantly carrying weapons (Noriko's knife and Ayane's various assortment of guns and swords).

I do feel like they're the same character, just with different quirks and places in the story. There are, of course, little things unique to each one of them, e.g. Ayane wanting to have a shit ton of kids and Noriko being an idealistic rebel with creative (musical) drive. But these are details, and I feel like the only real differences are circumstantial - their situations being different. Noriko's story seems to be about unreciprocated (yet) love, being a martyr and a constant second place, and her keeping her rightiousness and idealism in spite of this. Ayane, I feel, is more about loving in the face of adversity - blackmail, cheating, competition.

And I wouldn't say that there is something wrong with these two having the same basic characteristics - unique situations are enough for their stories to play out differently and in an entertaining way. I'm just trying to sort out my own confusion about this, as I feel like I enjoy Noriko the most out of all the characters, yet there is Ayane, who is nearly identical to her in most regards, but she is somehow a bit lower on my tierlist.
What do you people think?

Random theory time: Tsuneyo is Yasu, but with a good (or at least stubborn) parent

From the first chapter, we remember that dragons are not real. It does not mean a lot itself, but Tsuneyo immediately accepts the truth and avoids any questions about it. We can, of course, blame some small trauma, such as visitors making fun of her naivety, but when we remember who her father is and who their customers are, it does not sound convincing enough.

Then, in the third chapter we have a storyline when Tsuneyo gets to the RAS party, then tells Maya and Ayane that there was no party, "remembers" amusment park before sixth reset, and finnaly tells Sensei in chapter 4, that she thought that said party was a "dream", but she finnally convinced that it was real.

It makes me think that Tsuneyo is not just weird because of reclusive homeschooling, but has a real mental disorder (feels like dissociative one) and had been homeschooled because of that. And homeschooled well: she is high functioning, she uses logic to distinguish "dreams" from reality and ready to assume she is wrong and get help. She even built up specific sence of humor just to mask her inability to understand what is real and what is not on intuitive level.

Given that, her love and respect to her father is not a Stockholm syndrome. Her father took responsibility, raised her an helped with her mental illness, as an opposite to Yasu's parents. It is a hell of good job.

Bonus conclusion: if we assume, that Tsuneyo's problems are the same as Yasu's, they might have same "bad days". I.e. Tsuneyo has desapeared when Yasu broke during last update, etc, etc. I think there were more evidences, but cannot bring them out my head

posts.content_html_raw:
How I feel mentally when Niki is called Nikki for some reason:
Niki - "FUCK THE COCA-COLA!"

What I do about it:

Btw, just since it hasn't seemed to come up, on top of having Sensei recall his name, she also has him recall the place the accident happened, and it was Niki's letters delivered by Noriko that actually brought back Sensei's first confirmed memory of the past, which happened to be the night he first kissed Niki:
Teen Sensei - "Then why are you blushing so much?"
Niki - "That was the first night we kissed."
- "So that's what you remembered before anything else, huh?"

Niki definitely seems to fit the one true love cliché better than anyone. It's probably why Maya Prime and New Maya both feel threatened by her:
Niki - "We were meant for each other. I know it."
Maya Prime - "I'm in a bad mood. And feeling quite vulnerable, at that."
Long Maya - "But even with that being said...there is one other person I can't help but feel jealous of. Even if I think I am superior to them in basically every single way."
Sensei - "Is it...Niki?"
Shapeshifter Maya - "That's correct."

Noriko - "Hey, Ami, is Akira still-"
Niki - "What the fuck was that about?"
Sensei - "If I tell you it's because of Niki, will that be enough to make you leave?"
New Maya - "D..."
- "Don't even joke about that..."
- "You know how I feel about her. And we agreed that we wouldn't-"
She's his childhood best friend, first real girlfriend (kind of hard to count Sekai), and is seemingly only rivaled by Chika (Miss Maximum) in sexual compatibility with Sensei. Currently she's taking care of Sensei's niece and might even move in.

New Maya is in for a brutal awakening once she realizes what Sensei's been up to. Chika and Maya (in particular) are kind of Niki blind at the moment, but we'll see for how long.

posts.content_html_raw:
DeSkel15 said:
That's a peculiar way to flatter someone, and even then, Sensei just ignored it. He wasn't flattered. Ayane also ends up being surprised by Sensei sleeping with others, not noticing Molly was jealous of Otoha, not doing anything when Maya cried, and she doesn't really seem to understand anyone when it comes down to it. Ami, Makoto, Maya, Sana, Sensei, etc. Keep in mind that she thought Sana was completely innocent and pure, when that's just an act. Her answer to Ami's problems is also simply violence.

Empathy requires accuracy or it's not actually empathy. It's about understanding and feeling what others feel. Overcoming it together. Being wrong about what someone is feeling, shows a lack of understanding. Ayane thinks she understands others, yet never really does, which speaks for itself.

That card was actually Chika's idea to get Sensei to come back. Ayane mentioning others, especially Maya, was just to get what she wanted in the end, Sensei back. She's definitely not trying to get Maya and Sensei together. Ayane was simply out of ideas and was hoping for a miracle the night before.

Ayane also can't stop others from pursuing Sensei. Sensei goes to them, and even if she tried, that'd mess up her relationship with Sensei. That hasn't stopped her from secretly slapping Ami, trying to cuck Maya on the roof, and fucking him on both Ami's and Sana's beds behind their back, though.

Sympathy and empathy are different things. For example, Makoto isn't really bothered by Maya, like Ayane was. Ayane can understand being belittled by Maya, but not how being belittled by Maya actually makes others feel.

Ayane's kind of earned Ami's disdain (most have at this point). Lying to her, intentionally leaving her out of things, trying to fuck the man she loves on her bed, etc.

Early Chapter 4 Ami reached her breaking point, which has likely been building up since Sensei let slip he carried stuff at night for Maya back in Chapter 1. At least. From Ami's point of view, her friends have continuously been betraying her and endangering the only family she has left, for a long time, behind her back, and nothing she does can stop it or him, from hurting himself and her. It's not just Sensei who broke her. Everyone's been hurting her:
View attachment 3585382 Ami - "You see, you hurt me a lot. All of you have been hurting me lately. It's like you have a collective fetish for making cute redheads sad. And I try not to kink shame, but I'm not a big fan of that one."
Imagine if your best friends were sneaking around, fucking, and endangering your love interest that you do virtually everything for. One wrong move could lead to them being locked away. That's more or less Ami's life.

Just add voices, delusions, blackouts, more or less raising that adult love interest as a kid, and ptsd from watching your parents be taken from you, on top of it. This world also likely plays a factor. She seems aware of how things don't make sense, and are usually repetitive.

Overall: Ami has been driven insane and recently reached a breaking point. Ayane helped her get here.
Click to expand...
I feel like you've read between the lines. Annotated it. Read between the lines of your own annotation. Then did that again to arrive at a far-fetched cynical conclusion that Ayane is both sinister and doesn't understand anyone. Ayane being caring isn't some secret I'm uncovering. It's very plainly stated in the game and takes some intense mental gymnastics to overcome. Heck, in the last two scenes we've seen of Ayane we see her concerned about Yasu and Io and have a lengthy conversation with Sana about how she feels.
Your rebuttal of Ayane's card doesn't hold up when you consider her conversation with new Maya right after the reset where she basically tells Maya the same thing. Shes not out of ideas. Acknowledging Sensei and Maya's relationship and pain is literally her go to after Sensei starts to break.

And I know this is semantics at this point but empathy is not being a hyper observant detective. Its about sharing the emotions that are presented to you. For example, Nodoka explaining the way Io feels doesn't remotely make her empathetic. That's the entire point of that scene. Molly breaking down at the beach and having others share in that pain IS empathy.
This is like saying someone doesn't understand english because they can't understand you muttering under your breath. Nah, that guy is fluent. You're just not communicating.

This is all really straying far from my original point. It wasn't my intention to rank a character's ability to understand others. I would have chosen a different word had I known so much emphasis was going to be put on it. My point is, right now, Ami, Maya, and Ayane's friendship is dysfunctional. Indirectly, it's because of Sensei. Directly, it's because the relationship is currently completely one sided from every angle you look at it.

I appreciate the points you make. Sorry if any of this came off as heated.

throwing some thoughts here as well, not very streamlined as I need some time to reorg most of them but here goes:

Initially I thought the place they stumbled upon was something I could only call an "Angel Room", but the whole segment gave me very strong The Truman Show vibes, almost like they temporarily got into a show preparation room and saw the truth behind this weird world they're in, before getting promptly forced out.

Btw, what I read from the the writing on the book is:
T-84
Remote work is proceeding normally. Status: reversed. All subjects display heightened of individuality, yet remain ambitious in the face of uncertain tragedy. Thesis proceeding as expected.

I don't actually know what this means other than trying to force it onto my Truman Show hypothesis; why this feels somewhat important though is because the content of this book gets pixelated first before the whole frame does, as if the game was trying to hide it.

1. Despite the second map really looking like it is USER2's work that would lead Kaori to salvation with Nao's help, I'd say it's still too soon to say the first map that led Kaori to Nao was also from USER2.

Nao's answer to her origin by drawing an impregnated star, and Kaori's response to what she did with her own gold star make me feel like it is Kaori's wish that spawns Nao. Of course there has to be some divine play in the process of making Nao come true, but I am not confident enough to say the first treasure hunt was for sure USER2's work.

2. I am actually with Plant#1 on this, that it is unclear whether it was Nao who killed the plants or not. You can see her in shock when they exploded one by one, and I find it hard to believe it's Nao's doing. Though the way it ended is indeed interesting, it's almost like removing the hosts with external forces leads to both Sensei and Nao fall "out of bound" and thus couldn't be located by the system (not sure which one of them is TEMPLATE9 though).

As for this TV show itself, last time this setting was used by youdidit and Moyo who hosted the show back in Good Boy, so by association it'd be more HOPE/USER1 but these two Maya variants are also self-proclaimed "freelancers", so there might not be a specific god that is always responsible for these wretched shows.

3. Pareidolia is USER3, evident from Trinity Pt3 where USER3 conversed his concern with all lower case texts, so it doesn't look like it's him who puts everything back to place afterwards. Also I have some doubt whether it is USER2 who restores TEMPLATE9. I think the style "////////CAPSLOCK" is also used by "general system messages" that don't pertain to any specific god, but I could be in the wrong here. Plus, USER2 restoring something from USER4 sounds like a divinely overstepping and unprecedent move if each USER corresponds to a god or something of a similar level.

But I'm just kinda excited about the the very first time we see something that involves USER4.

You're totally right about USER3, I forgot that. So i went back, and i think there are a few interesting things about the moment that nao-chan gets "lost" that I overlooked:


1. It's not nao-chan that
gets lost, it's both of them! Or maybe she drags him there (since he doesn't remember getting there, and she's already awake), i don't know. But it's definitely both that are there.

2. Where is there exactly?
And I think it's beyond the city limits, and if I had to bet it's where Himawari/Daisy/etc finds and rescues Akira from previously - this would corroborate why there are those flowers on the ground and the Himawarico. That would also reinforce that, at least in this particular case, USER4 is Himawari.
3. Another thing of note is: Is this even
nao-chan? or is this Himawari herself? Nao-chan doesn't answer if it's her obviously, but there are plenty of weird things in this setup, including her reaction and overall positioning between the two that could suggest it's not her (although it's a given this is the weakest theory here, it could just be that she's scared, or that she realised something about herself).

4. And about Template 9,
I wonder if we may be thinking about it wrong. Maybe Template 9 is neither of them, but the actual city. Like, we're right now on setting 9 of how the city and its puppets should operate, and somehow what they did broke the setting, and thus they ended up outside the regulated template. But then they used Himawari's backup of the city itself to restore it.

This could go with the reason as to why there were those people behind the doors regulating the setting and running experiments, and could also explain why Himawari can more or less freely operate but doesn't have much power since she's an outsider (?).

There are a lot of random ideas here, but i think there may be some merit regarding where they ended up and Himawari's involvement.

Also, yes, i'm really happy about seeing USER4 doing something, and one can hope at last we'll have someone on Akira's side.

Phew! Finally done with 0.40! Gather 'round the campfire with me and let's get into some thoughts on the update.

- I enjoyed the change of scenery a lot, actually. I didn't think a camping setting sounded very appealing at first, but y'know what? It was a nice escape from the typical setting of the city of Kumon-mi.
- I said it in a post earlier as I was playing, but I LOVE that Akira is actually making an actual effort for Ami as not just her guardian, but an actual father. The scene where he sat her down and admitted he fucked up showed immense growth on his part. More on Dad Akira and Daughter Ami in a bit.
Sensei - "Why is everything I don't want to happen suddenly happening in very quick succession? Are even my inner monologues not safe anymore?"
Pareidolia - "lmaoooooooooo"
Sensei Narrator - "Oh, come on."

- Pareidolia, you're such a fucking asshole, dude. But I will say this: you certainly are entertaining.
Yuki - "Jesus, fuck! Stop!"

- CUTE!!! As was this entire conversation, save the parts about cannibalism. Yuki may not wanna admit it, but she's beginning to fall for Akira too. Oh the obstacles that are Sara and Yumi... I can't say I don't understand her hesitation for taking things further at this current time. Things will have to change some more before things can proceed with the badass biker mom. Cracks are definitely showing in the armor of her resolve, though. That much is certain.

Wire God (?) - "//////////////////////USER 2 HAS CONNECTED VIA HOT SPOT
- "//////////////////////PLEASE ACCEPT THE CONNECTION BY-"
Pareidolia - "no. do not acccept that-"
HOPE (?) - "DO NOT OPEN THE DOOR"
Wire God (?) - "//////////////////////OPEN THE DOOR"
Pareidolia and HOPE (?) - "i FUCKING told YOU to NOT accept THAT fucking-"

- Imma be real, I'm not sure who the hell these voices are, although I have my guesses. We know the lowercase text is Pareidolia, and the all caps text is HOPE traditionally, whereas the slashes represent the Wire God. So perhaps then, it's the Wire God speaking to Akira in this moment after all and it isn't some form of trickery by text again? I dunno. I haven't read any other comments just yet, so I can only guess right now. I'm sure someone smarter than me can piece together something logical. Assuming what I believe to be true is correct, though, damn... kinda insane if ya think about it. We've never seen the gods this active before, speaking out at once. I guess their competition is growing even more fierce.
Nao - "..."
Sensei - "..."
- "What the fuck?"

- This doesn't appear in the replay at all. Nor does the scene outside the strange door either. This is a recurring theme with Nao-chan, I've noticed. It's almost like there's more to her than meets the eye or somethin'...
Nao - "!... (Star)"
- "!...... (Child)"

- Nao-chan is a star child confirmed! It kinda goes hand in hand with her sudden appearance in the first place and the Himawarico reference at the end of this very same event. Obviously a hint that Himawari is a star child herself.

Plant #2 - "I want to season Nao-chan's meat pocket with my special sauce."
Nao - "..."
Plant #1 - "Not cool, Plant #2. You knew exactly what that tweet was insinuating."
Plant #2 - "Yeah. But we can't deny how nice it was. And, you know what? I'm just gonna say it. I'd season her meat pocket as well."

- RIP Plant Council. Your demise was untimely and you will never be forgotten... I think Plant #2 spoke for all of us cultured wizard enthusiasts.
Ami - "You're doing great."
- "And I'm excited for you to keep being my dad for the rest of our lives."
Sensei - "..."
Ami - "..."
Sensei - "..."
Ami - "Is it...okay if I call you that now?..."
- "Dad?..."

- This scene had me all kinds of fucking emotional, man. We had the scene earlier in Ami's bedroom where Akira laid things out to her that he was gonna be better to her like she had been for him over the years before he invited her to the camping trip, and now Ami finally calls Akira 'Dad' for real. It took 4 chapters, and we of course know Akira is far from perfect, but goddamn if this wasn't a satisfying payoff for me...

Akira not only makes some big strides as a character, taking Ami's needs into consideration for once, but now Ami can finally have someone to rely on too. Sure, their relationship is still... pretty fucked up all things considered, but I mean... progress is progress, right?

Also, the fact Ami just straight up told Akira 'hey, what if you're actually my dad?' is both kinda shocking and kinda funny to me at the same time lol. It isn't surprising at all that she still had incestuous feelings for him, even though he's mooooost likely her actual father.


- Oh, and look! He SMILED! It's a rare, genuine Akira smile! Ya love to see it...


- Dat ass.


- Touka, you naughty slut! You've gotten brazen as hell this update, haven't you?
Sara - "I think the four of us could have a nice life together."
Sensei - "..."
Ami - "Dad?"
Sensei - "I think we need to have another talk soon, Ami."

- Hooooo boy. This complicates matters. First we have Niki wanting to move in, and now we have Sara wanting the same thing. Combine that with the fact that Ami loves Sensei romantically too, and Sana has been opposed to Sensei in the role as her father since Chapter 1 (not to mention she's also sexually active with him now too), things are gonna get very messy.

Akira has been slowly tangling more and more wires around himself, between this Niki and Sara business, the Ami situation, fucking New Maya at his apartment where Chika ran into her the next day... It's allll gonna come back to bite him in the ass at some point. Just a matter of when the storm is gonna arrive.

"74 68 69 73 20 69 73 20 6e 6f 74 20 68 65 72"
"this is not her"

- No clue if anyone else has gotten to this yet, but it's new to me and I wanted to try my hand at translating these hexadecimals, so here ya go! Kinda cool, albeit a bit depressing as well. But what else is new?
Touka - "Well, would you look at that? It's only been forty-five minutes, Sensei. Were you so excited to see me that you left early?"

- Touka is sassy as hell lately and I am all for that! Also, hey! She's still drinking that boxed green tea that Sensei forced her to drink from that very same first vending machine she had them meet at for their date. That's cute, actually.

- The mommy issues are staggering... Love the renders, though, even if Sekai's is on screen for like a fraction of a second.
Sensei - "Stop interfering."
Tsubasa - "Will there be consequences if I don't?"
Sensei - "Probably not. But stop anyway."
Tsubasa - "Shame. I like consequences."

- Ooooooooooh, I can't wait to fucking punish Tsubasa one of these days... Getting sick of her high and mighty demeanor. Plus, she deliberately put Touka in a bad mood. For what purpose? I can only imagine... My theory, though, is she intentionally created a situation in which Touka was upset so Akira would be forced to comfort her. Other than that, I mean, that's all I got.

The day we get leverage on Tsubasa will be a very happy day, indeed. I await with great anticipation.
Touka - "So...what do we do now? Mother is bound to ask what transpired in here when I see her in the morning."
Sensei - "If you really wanna fuck with her, just tell her we had sex."
Touka - "Sensei! I couldn't possibly-"
Sensei - "Stop."
- "Call me Akira from now on."

- And now yet another student knows Sensei's real name! Honestly, I found the gesture really endearing. It shows he trusts Touka a lot and will no doubt positively impact their relationship moving forward. Speaking of... it's rather complicated, huh? Touka knows Akira sees her as a mother figure, but... is also aroused by her, and it seems they're willing to tackle both at once. Time will tell what's in store for the two of them. All I know is Touka has been horny as hellll this update! XD Even she isn't immune to the Sensei withdrawals.

Y'know, I have to wonder how Ayane will take this, assuming she finds out. Which I mean, we've already established that Akira is tying himself up in a web of problems, so she very well could. We still have the cliffhanger involving Sana from the latest Dorm Wars, and now that the heir of the richest family in Kumon-mi is getting involved with her 'future husband'? It has to be getting to her mentally, yeah? Especially with the apocalypse shit happening at the same time.

Guess we'll see. We're due for a reset soon, anyway.
Molly - "It is nice to be cherished, yes."
- "But sometimes I wish that you'd just break me already."
Pareidolia - "oh shit."

- Agreed, Pareidolia. Agreed.
- Molly's h scene in the dorms was pretty good. The possibilities for all the different cosplay are endless... And really, I mean, I'm just glad she got some time to shine here. She's had horrific luck in terms of love, so to see the Irish lass feeling good about herself for a change? It was nice.
- Haruka's last event was kinda meh. Sucks that Molly just left a note and dipped. Was hoping there'd be more to it than that. I guess it's cool she's still an obedient slave, though.
- Kaori was Kaori tbh. Not sure what to feel about her events. Nao-chan stole the show this update in comparison. Kaori just felt a little out of her element here, I suppose.

All things considered, solid update! Loved it a lot! It's nice to see Akira with more screen time again (FINALLY!) and things slowly getting back on track. We had some memorable moments this update... my favorite of which of course being where Ami calls Akira her Dad. It may take some getting used to, but y'know what? I like it. I hope it sticks around.

Thank you for reading my long ass review! Now it's time for me to catch back up with the forum. XD

1. I agree that one of the best part of this update was Akira's growth. There was a moment where I legit stopped and said to myself "yeah, cause you really really love Ami." Like, in the most simple and basic definition of the word, he loves her. And it's such a powerful thing too, cause it's not a reaction to Sekai's abuse, his coping, his nothing - it's just that he loves his family. That doesn't mean that everything else isn't fucked up, or that he'll be able to actually be better, but there's a light somewhere and it's genuine and heartwarming to realise that even at this point with everything that happened, this remains inside of him.


I have a question about that scene actually, cause i thought for a moment if that couldn't mean that Ami is kinda of out of his sphere of command, because of her close connection to Sekai or Hope. But maybe I read too much into it.

It was so cute to realise she reacts in the exact same way her daughter does to it (minus feeling threatened by Akira, which lets everything flow much better). She's so bereft of affection and experience however that i think this bridge will be crossed without much effort at all. Yumi might not even care to be honest, nor Sara (which is her worry).

I'm assuming this is a battle between Wire God = USER2, and Pareidolia = USER3. It's been pointed out that maybe Wire God was trying to help Kaori with this treasure hunt. I'd like to know more about the star child thing, I haven't made sense of it at all. Maybe they are beings that were born outside of the simulation? And that they're inside of it is the explanation why they shouldn't exist/can move somewhat freely?

I also haven't seen much about the colors, that Kaori mentions. And if so, maybe wire god was trying to purge kaori of sekai by leading her there?

Cause if he just kept being a jackass to everyone, then everyone would be kept at a distance more or less, but as he becomes more decent, everything will clash. This Sara thing was VERY forward in my opinion, I mean it's understandable that she went for it, since so many people are going to go for it - but man, it's a lot to throw into someone's face since it more or less it's a declaration that she's having sex with Akira, directly to Ami's face.

1. I agree that one of the best part of this update was Akira's growth. There was a moment where I legit stopped and said to myself "yeah, cause you really really love Ami." Like, in the most simple and basic definition of the word, he loves her. That doesn't mean that everything else isn't fucked up, or that he'll be able to actually be better, but there's a light somewhere and it's genuine and heartwarming to realise that even at this point with everything that happened, this remains inside of him.

Nao stuff and colors
I'm assuming this is a battle between Wire God = USER2, and Pareidolia = USER3. It's been pointed out that maybe Wire God was trying to help Kaori with this treasure hunt. But given what they find inside of the door, it might as well have been an attempt to simply crush Pareidolia's season, since Nao and Akira pretty much break the world and they have to restore it through USER4 = Himawari.
I'd like to know more about the star child thing, I haven't made sense of it at all. Maybe they are beings that were born outside of the simulation? And that they're inside of it is the explanation why they shouldn't exist/can move somewhat freely?
I also haven't seen much about the colors, that Kaori mentions. She seemed to think that the door would lead to something that would regulate colors, and that she's green on the outside and red on the inside (maya and sekai?). And if so, maybe wire god was trying to purge kaori of sekai by leading her there?
Spoiler:
Touka cellphone
For a second during the cellphone scene I wondered if Touka was actually masturbating while talking to him...
Spoiler:
Ami we need to talk
I think there's a possibility that we may very well be led into the dark route by his attempt to do good. Cause if he just kept being a jackass to everyone, then everyone would be kept at a distance more or less, but as he becomes more decent, everything will clash. This Sara thing was VERY forward in my opinion, I mean it's understandable that she went for it, since so many people are going to go for it - but man, it's a lot to throw into someone's face since it more or less it's a declaration that she's having sex with Akira, directly to Ami's face.
And i mean, i have nothing against Sara, but she never had a chance in hell. Having her and Sana move into a house with those two shortly after all that happened? That's delusional.
Spoiler:
Touka uses name
So the thing about Touka is that, in the first place, i wonder if her mother actually intended for them to quarrel and thus facilitate them having sex. Cause if things followed the way they had, there was a chance Akira would hesitate since she knew he saw her as a mother figure, and by having Touka confront him with that, she probably knew he'd strike back with "yeah, and I'd fuck you regardless". Then again, she's very murky to me, I understand her wanting for Touka to break her heart in a controlled environment, but what's the deal with the little sister then?
Also, the thing about Akira telling Touka to call him by his name froze my blood. Cause I didn't interpret it as a good thing, but a full-on regression to Sekai's relationship. Most likely this will end up with her calling him Aki-kun (as Sekai does when he comes back home).
Spoiler:
Molly and Haruka
I loved Molly's events. Give the girl what she wants already, and given that we're coming from rape that happened and then was erased, the current developments are way cuter than they had any reason to be, and I'm here for it. Weirdly enough, I could actually see them becoming an item.
Haruka's was... I don't know to be honest. Cause Molly's event was very wholesome, I'm strangely glad that she wasn't there for Haruka to be a predator. And it's weird cause, okay maybe bizarre take here, but Akira before realising the world was resetting did not act predatorial to a single person other than Maya, and that was a very special case in which we're not sure what happened exactly (Maya could have even initiated or blackmailed him for all we know). Whilst Haruka has no idea resets occur, and yet keeps employees that she herself says she should fire, just because she wants to have sex with them AND SEXUALLY HARASSES them by sending nude pictures. I mean, call me weird, but I want her to be with Nodoka and Kirin, not wholesome people.

Just some food for thought, since this comment gives me an excuse to evaluate things a little:
"He foreshadows that she's this lunatic psychotic killer that tortured everyone"

That was Maya Prime who implied this. And that was after Tsuneyo pointed out that Maya Prime's memories aren't anymore reliable than anyone elses, and she's kind of always been a liar, on top of this, then The Shapeshifter later seemed to debunk Psycho Ami as a thing:
Tsuneyo - "Why should everyone trust you just because you say you've been around the longest when you've already admitted to the possibility of false memories being swapped in for the truth?"
- "You are no more reliable than I am...but you want to be seen that way. And the people who want trust the most are, more often than not, the ones who are not meant to be trusted."
Maya - "I lie to you literally all the time. I don't think this should come as that big of a surprise."
- "In here, I'm just as bad as you. I only give a shit about two people- and I've lied to one of them more times than I can even count."
Shapeshifter/Himawari - "She really won't hurt you."
Even if Maya wasn't lying, she has a habit of simply being wrong throughout the game. Ami herself also hasn't really hurt anyone or tried to. Besides herself, and accidentally Sensei, after she loses it later.

Conclusion: Psycho Ami never really had any ground to stand on, beyond Ami not being mentally well. Albeit, very few people in this game are mentally well.

"follows up a bit on it after with her gaslighting her friends and trying to scare Ayane into submission."

It was actually Maya Prime who scared Ayane. She's the one who told her about the Ami stuff, and the one who told Ayane that Ami wanted them to go to the shrine for some reason. Ami apparently didn't call or text Ayane about this and only did Maya. That whole thing was only between Ami and Maya. Ayane just got dragged along for some reason:
Ayane - "How is any of this my fault?! I was just trying to watch a movie when you barged in and started yelling stuff about Ami!"
Ami actually seemed to feel sad because of Ayane being scared of her:
Ami - "I'd just rather sit here for now if that's okay. I don't...think Ayane wants to talk to me at the moment."
And if Ami is having sex with Sensei, she offers to share him with Ayane to make her feel better:
Ami - "Do you want to share him?"
- "I was really hoping I wouldn't have to. But if that's what it takes to rekindle our friendship, I guess I can learn to deal with it."

"Then Ayane snaps out of it and gives Ami a good talk which makes you think she'd change for the better, and she starts to actually get better giving us a breather instead of constantly being on our back"

Ayane actually just slaps around her best friend and tells her to do what she wants, or she'll keep hitting her:
Ayane - "No one is bullying you. Or being mean to you. Or trying to force you out of anything. And if you're going to keep spouting immature complaints like that, I'm going to keep hitting you."
She was also gaslighting Ami here. No one is bullying or being mean to you, she says after slapping her and threatening to again. Then saying no one is forcing Ami out of anything while literally going behind her back and trying to keep her from finding out about the resets. She at least admits Ami was being left out when Ami isn't around to hear it:
Ayane - "If anything, I think tonight might be a good way for her to start feeling included again after being left out of so much important stuff. So I say we just try to have fun."
A little bit after hitting her on the beach.

I'm not sure how this could lead to things getting better, Ami-wise. Ayane was happier I guess. Ami just had another reason to lose her mind, and ended up laughing somewhat maniacally afterwards.

Ami was also actually trying to be less clingy before this, as well. Ever since the Psycho Ami stuff, she was trying to give Sensei space, albeit it probably started when Sensei told her to stop suffocating him:
Sensei - "And I'd appreciate it if you'd stop suffocating me."
Ami - "..."
A little before the Psycho Ami stuff.

Conclusion on both: Ami seems to have been getting isolated by the plot, in various ways, and being alone is her greatest fear:
Sensei - "Is being alone something you're afraid of?"
Ami - "Without really getting into it...it's probably my biggest fear of all."
Maya and Sensei have also been leaving Ami out of things since well before the resets (secret relationship), then after Ayane starts a relationship with Sensei, this probably added to it, and after Ayane reached the roof, they all started leaving her out of things, in a rather obvious way, that she simply couldn't ignore anymore. This left her alone with the voices in her head/god:

Angiboat said:
It was good stuff but I got the feeling that Selebus had no idea about what he wanted to do with Ami. Her character was all over the place with the last 4-6 updates.
He foreshadows that she's this lunatic psychotic killer that tortured everyone including Sensei follows up a bit on it after with her gaslighting her friends and trying to scare Ayane into submission.

Then Ayane snaps out of it and gives Ami a good talk which makes you think she'd change for the better, and she starts to actually get better giving us a breather instead of constantly being on our back, only for it to immediately be gone and she absolutely shuts everyone out, even her closest friends.
Click to expand...
I dont really see this that critical. I dont know if you ever had really toxic people with severe mental problems in your life. But stuff like this is actually pretty common. They promise to do better, they tell you they will improve. And even when they actually ment that genuine, after a while they still continue with the old toxic behavour they just have been called out for, as if they never had been called out. So in that way, when you look at realism Ami is actually pretty consistent. And it was even what i did expect to happen.

Okay i was sort of surprised it actually did needed his whole break down to become this bad, because i was expecting that this would happen with her without even thinking about anything like that. But on the other hand i wasnt surprised at all that she did reach out to Niki and none of her friends for help. Because i would assume from her perspective she burned all bridges with her old friends, so of course she needed someone else entirely.

And in that regard i am actually still a bit surprised about her conversation with Maya. Because in the end it was pretty obvious that she just acted tired to give the excuse to leave her right away. I mean from the whole conversation it is imo pretty clear that she is fully aware why Maya did come to visit and it was not because of her. And that of course she wanted to leave again after she got the information she wanted to get.

I think this could mean that she tries again to do better. To improve again. To rebuild the burned bridges. I mean i have read the posts that believe this might be a trap and maya made a big mistake with that promise and all that. But i am not convinced. I dont think it is part of a big plan. But more like the usual loop of people like her. She wants to do better and in the end will still fall into the same old tracks.

DeSkel15 said:
Just some food for thought, since this comment gives me an excuse to evaluate things a little:
"He foreshadows that she's this lunatic psychotic killer that tortured everyone"

That was Maya Prime who implied this. And that was after Tsuneyo pointed out that Maya Prime's memories aren't anymore reliable than anyone elses, and she's kind of always been a liar, on top of this, then The Shapeshifter later seemed to debunk Psycho Ami as a thing:
View attachment 3597759 View attachment 3597757 View attachment 3597749 View attachment 3597874 View attachment 3597765 Tsuneyo - "Why should everyone trust you just because you say you've been around the longest when you've already admitted to the possibility of false memories being swapped in for the truth?"
- "You are no more reliable than I am...but you want to be seen that way. And the people who want trust the most are, more often than not, the ones who are not meant to be trusted."
Maya - "I lie to you literally all the time. I don't think this should come as that big of a surprise."
- "In here, I'm just as bad as you. I only give a shit about two people- and I've lied to one of them more times than I can even count."
Shapeshifter/Himawari - "She really won't hurt you."
Even if Maya wasn't lying, she has a habit of simply being wrong throughout the game. Ami herself also hasn't really hurt anyone or tried to. Besides herself, and accidentally Sensei, after she loses it later.

Conclusion: Psycho Ami never really had any ground to stand on, beyond Ami not being mentally well. Albeit, very few people in this game are mentally well.

"follows up a bit on it after with her gaslighting her friends and trying to scare Ayane into submission."

It was actually Maya Prime who scared Ayane. She's the one who told her about the Ami stuff, and the one who told Ayane that Ami wanted them to go to the shrine for some reason. Ami apparently didn't call or text Ayane about this and only did Maya. That whole thing was only between Ami and Maya. Ayane just got dragged along for some reason:
View attachment 3598140 Ayane - "How is any of this my fault?! I was just trying to watch a movie when you barged in and started yelling stuff about Ami!"
Ami actually seemed to feel sad because of Ayane being scared of her:
View attachment 3598142 Ami - "I'd just rather sit here for now if that's okay. I don't...think Ayane wants to talk to me at the moment."
And if Ami is having sex with Sensei, she offers to share him with Ayane to make her feel better:
View attachment 3598161 View attachment 3598163 Ami - "Do you want to share him?"
- "I was really hoping I wouldn't have to. But if that's what it takes to rekindle our friendship, I guess I can learn to deal with it."

"Then Ayane snaps out of it and gives Ami a good talk which makes you think she'd change for the better, and she starts to actually get better giving us a breather instead of constantly being on our back"

Ayane actually just slaps around her best friend and tells her to do what she wants, or she'll keep hitting her:
View attachment 3597809 Ayane - "No one is bullying you. Or being mean to you. Or trying to force you out of anything. And if you're going to keep spouting immature complaints like that, I'm going to keep hitting you."
She was also gaslighting Ami here. No one is bullying or being mean to you, she says after slapping her and threatening to again. Then saying no one is forcing Ami out of anything while literally going behind her back and trying to keep her from finding out about the resets. She at least admits Ami was being left out when Ami isn't around to hear it:
View attachment 3597817 Ayane - "If anything, I think tonight might be a good way for her to start feeling included again after being left out of so much important stuff. So I say we just try to have fun."
A little bit after hitting her on the beach.

I'm not sure how this could lead to things getting better, Ami-wise. Ayane was happier I guess. Ami just had another reason to lose her mind, and ended up laughing somewhat maniacally afterwards.

Ami was also actually trying to be less clingy before this, as well. Ever since the Psycho Ami stuff, she was trying to give Sensei space, albeit it probably started when Sensei told her to stop suffocating him:
View attachment 3597728 View attachment 3597730 Sensei - "And I'd appreciate it if you'd stop suffocating me."
Ami - "..."
A little before the Psycho Ami stuff.

Conclusion on both: Ami seems to have been getting isolated by the plot, in various ways, and being alone is her greatest fear:
View attachment 3597979 View attachment 3597981 Sensei - "Is being alone something you're afraid of?"
Ami - "Without really getting into it...it's probably my biggest fear of all."
Maya and Sensei have also been leaving Ami out of things since well before the resets (secret relationship), then after Ayane starts a relationship with Sensei, this probably added to it, and after Ayane reached the roof, they all started leaving her out of things, in a rather obvious way, that she simply couldn't ignore anymore. This left her alone with the voices in her head/god:
View attachment 3597994 View attachment 3597995 View attachment 3597992 Sensei - "Probably just the voices inside of your head or something."
Ami - "I don't think so. Those are a lot less reserved."
- "There are a million girls trying to trick you into believing we're not meant to be together, but I have talked to God and he says that we are."
Possibly is referring to Pareidolia here, since it's all about voices, being called a god, and causing drama, albeit, it may be unrelated.

"only for it to immediately be gone and she absolutely shuts everyone out, even her closest friends."

Ami gets butchered, seemingly reset, then Sensei breaks, and she spends the next 2 months wiping his ass. Ami actually wanted to be with her "friends":
View attachment 3597901 Ami - "It hurts a little, you know. Having to be the bad guy, I mean. It'd be great to let everybody back into the house again. It'd be great being able to go to the Christmas party."
Sensei has just made it clear to her he doesn't want others around him when it comes to fixing his mental health:
View attachment 3597903 View attachment 3597907 Sensei - "I know if I was trying to fix my mental health, the last thing I'd want is a bunch of people showing up at my door and trying to force me to feel better."
Ami - "Sensei just needs a little more time by himself until he's feeling confident and safe enough to leave his room! And I, his beloved niece, am doing everything in my power to help with that!"

Then people break into her house, making her feel like a failure who can't keep Sensei safe:
View attachment 3597904 View attachment 3597905 Ami - "I know! I'm sorry! I shouldn't have left you! I thought they'd be at the party! I didn't expect them to come here! Not today!"
- "You're right. It isn't safe here anymore..."
This is what really seemed to mess her up. Showing her she's imperfect and that they aren't safe. Finding Uta's wizard pic, and all the other stuff from the girls probably didn't help. Sensei then wakes up earlier than he's supposed to, and as soon as possible blows her off, leaving her alone, eventually leading to the scissors stuff which causes her to break, and become bedridden.

Ami still hasn't actually shut anyone out, though. New Maya and Niki have visited her. Ayane and Sana, etc, just don't really care, while Sensei has tried to keep whoever does, out of it, because that's how he handles things, and thinks that's how Ami wants to handle things...without asking her, because he's Sensei. Hence Ami calling Niki for help, after Sensei told Niki to stay out of it, which causes Sensei to throw a tantrum at Niki:
View attachment 3598143 View attachment 3598144 Sensei - "STOP FUCKING AROUND!"
Niki - "Akira...you are not allowed to yell at me like that. That was not okay."

Conclusion: Ami is broken down as much as possible, and gives up on taking care of herself and Sensei at the moment. She seems to mostly just dream and talk to herself/voices during this time.

"This camping event was a nice one but again, where the hell is this going? I don't want to be lead on again like when she was starting to get mature to immediately devolve."

Sara is giving Ami a mother figure and possibly a sister figure (similar could be said for Niki). Sensei is accepting his place as a father figure. Ami is changing the way she sees herself, and seems to be recovering enough to leave her room. Possibly allowing herself to live for herself instead of others.

Conclusion: Ami might actually be growing for the first time since she was like 7, and lost her parents.

Sana however is getting sexual with Sensei (Sara and Ami are optional), so that'll probably play a factor in what's to come, especially since it's apparently Sana's Chapter. Sana seems open to sharing though, so it probably won't bother Ami that much.
Overall: If I were to guess, Sel probably just wants us to experience Ami's development within this environment, and it's effects on her and those around her. Lessons in loving the broken niece:
View attachment 3598228 View attachment 3598229 View attachment 3598230 View attachment 3598231
Click to expand...
I feel like you're Ami's biggest supporter in this entire game, and after this update and your comment, I'm 100% sure that Ami will stay stuck in my top 2 for many updates.

I really have to do a full replay instead of just going back and looking at events. I noticed that the eyes changed, but never that there were eyes specific to specific gods. Sekai was also with Akira during the Sana thing though, and controlled Kaori.

Oh, I have a question regarding Sara though: She mentions she's afraid of the darkness most of all or something like that, but I don't recall HOPE being associated with that (?)
Click to expand...

Just some food for thought, since this comment gives me an excuse to evaluate things a little:
"He foreshadows that she's this lunatic psychotic killer that tortured everyone"

That was Maya Prime who implied this. And that was after Tsuneyo pointed out that Maya Prime's memories aren't anymore reliable than anyone elses, and she's kind of always been a liar, on top of this, then The Shapeshifter later seemed to debunk Psycho Ami as a thing:
View attachment 3597759 View attachment 3597757 View attachment 3597749 View attachment 3597874 View attachment 3597765 Tsuneyo - "Why should everyone trust you just because you say you've been around the longest when you've already admitted to the possibility of false memories being swapped in for the truth?"
- "You are no more reliable than I am...but you want to be seen that way. And the people who want trust the most are, more often than not, the ones who are not meant to be trusted."
Maya - "I lie to you literally all the time. I don't think this should come as that big of a surprise."
- "In here, I'm just as bad as you. I only give a shit about two people- and I've lied to one of them more times than I can even count."
Shapeshifter/Himawari - "She really won't hurt you."
Even if Maya wasn't lying, she has a habit of simply being wrong throughout the game. Ami herself also hasn't really hurt anyone or tried to. Besides herself, and accidentally Sensei, after she loses it later.

Conclusion: Psycho Ami never really had any ground to stand on, beyond Ami not being mentally well. Albeit, very few people in this game are mentally well.

"follows up a bit on it after with her gaslighting her friends and trying to scare Ayane into submission."

It was actually Maya Prime who scared Ayane. She's the one who told her about the Ami stuff, and the one who told Ayane that Ami wanted them to go to the shrine for some reason. Ami apparently didn't call or text Ayane about this and only did Maya. That whole thing was only between Ami and Maya. Ayane just got dragged along for some reason:
View attachment 3598140 Ayane - "How is any of this my fault?! I was just trying to watch a movie when you barged in and started yelling stuff about Ami!"
Ami actually seemed to feel sad because of Ayane being scared of her:
View attachment 3598142 Ami - "I'd just rather sit here for now if that's okay. I don't...think Ayane wants to talk to me at the moment."
And if Ami is having sex with Sensei, she offers to share him with Ayane to make her feel better:
View attachment 3598161 View attachment 3598163 Ami - "Do you want to share him?"
- "I was really hoping I wouldn't have to. But if that's what it takes to rekindle our friendship, I guess I can learn to deal with it."

"Then Ayane snaps out of it and gives Ami a good talk which makes you think she'd change for the better, and she starts to actually get better giving us a breather instead of constantly being on our back"

Ayane actually just slaps around her best friend and tells her to do what she wants, or she'll keep hitting her:
View attachment 3597809 Ayane - "No one is bullying you. Or being mean to you. Or trying to force you out of anything. And if you're going to keep spouting immature complaints like that, I'm going to keep hitting you."
She was also gaslighting Ami here. No one is bullying or being mean to you, she says after slapping her and threatening to again. Then saying no one is forcing Ami out of anything while literally going behind her back and trying to keep her from finding out about the resets. She at least admits Ami was being left out when Ami isn't around to hear it:
View attachment 3597817 Ayane - "If anything, I think tonight might be a good way for her to start feeling included again after being left out of so much important stuff. So I say we just try to have fun."
A little bit after hitting her on the beach.

I'm not sure how this could lead to things getting better, Ami-wise. Ayane was happier I guess. Ami just had another reason to lose her mind, and ended up laughing somewhat maniacally afterwards.

Ami was also actually trying to be less clingy before this, as well. Ever since the Psycho Ami stuff, she was trying to give Sensei space, albeit it probably started when Sensei told her to stop suffocating him:
View attachment 3597728 View attachment 3597730 Sensei - "And I'd appreciate it if you'd stop suffocating me."
Ami - "..."
A little before the Psycho Ami stuff.

Conclusion on both: Ami seems to have been getting isolated by the plot, in various ways, and being alone is her greatest fear:
View attachment 3597979 View attachment 3597981 Sensei - "Is being alone something you're afraid of?"
Ami - "Without really getting into it...it's probably my biggest fear of all."
Maya and Sensei have also been leaving Ami out of things since well before the resets (secret relationship), then after Ayane starts a relationship with Sensei, this probably added to it, and after Ayane reached the roof, they all started leaving her out of things, in a rather obvious way, that she simply couldn't ignore anymore. This left her alone with the voices in her head/god:
View attachment 3597994 View attachment 3597995 View attachment 3597992 Sensei - "Probably just the voices inside of your head or something."
Ami - "I don't think so. Those are a lot less reserved."
- "There are a million girls trying to trick you into believing we're not meant to be together, but I have talked to God and he says that we are."
Possibly is referring to Pareidolia here, since it's all about voices, being called a god, and causing drama, albeit, it may be unrelated.

"only for it to immediately be gone and she absolutely shuts everyone out, even her closest friends."

Ami gets butchered, seemingly reset, then Sensei breaks, and she spends the next 2 months wiping his ass. Ami actually wanted to be with her "friends":
View attachment 3597901 Ami - "It hurts a little, you know. Having to be the bad guy, I mean. It'd be great to let everybody back into the house again. It'd be great being able to go to the Christmas party."
Sensei has just made it clear to her he doesn't want others around him when it comes to fixing his mental health:
View attachment 3597903 View attachment 3597907 Sensei - "I know if I was trying to fix my mental health, the last thing I'd want is a bunch of people showing up at my door and trying to force me to feel better."
Ami - "Sensei just needs a little more time by himself until he's feeling confident and safe enough to leave his room! And I, his beloved niece, am doing everything in my power to help with that!"

Then people break into her house, making her feel like a failure who can't keep Sensei safe:
View attachment 3597904 View attachment 3597905 Ami - "I know! I'm sorry! I shouldn't have left you! I thought they'd be at the party! I didn't expect them to come here! Not today!"
- "You're right. It isn't safe here anymore..."
This is what really seemed to mess her up. Showing her she's imperfect and that they aren't safe. Finding Uta's wizard pic, and all the other stuff from the girls probably didn't help. Sensei then wakes up earlier than he's supposed to, and as soon as possible blows her off, leaving her alone, eventually leading to the scissors stuff which causes her to break, and become bedridden.

Ami still hasn't actually shut anyone out, though. New Maya and Niki have visited her. Ayane and Sana, etc, just don't really care, while Sensei has tried to keep whoever does, out of it, because that's how he handles things, and thinks that's how Ami wants to handle things...without asking her, because he's Sensei. Hence Ami calling Niki for help, after Sensei told Niki to stay out of it, which causes Sensei to throw a tantrum at Niki:
View attachment 3598143 View attachment 3598144 Sensei - "STOP FUCKING AROUND!"
Niki - "Akira...you are not allowed to yell at me like that. That was not okay."

Conclusion: Ami is broken down as much as possible, and gives up on taking care of herself and Sensei at the moment. She seems to mostly just dream and talk to herself/voices during this time.

"This camping event was a nice one but again, where the hell is this going? I don't want to be lead on again like when she was starting to get mature to immediately devolve."

Sara is giving Ami a mother figure and possibly a sister figure (similar could be said for Niki). Sensei is accepting his place as a father figure. Ami is changing the way she sees herself, and seems to be recovering enough to leave her room. Possibly allowing herself to live for herself instead of others.

Conclusion: Ami might actually be growing for the first time since she was like 7, and lost her parents.

Sana however is getting sexual with Sensei (Sara and Ami are optional), so that'll probably play a factor in what's to come, especially since it's apparently Sana's Chapter. Sana seems open to sharing though, so it probably won't bother Ami that much.
Overall: If I were to guess, Sel probably just wants us to experience Ami's development within this environment, and it's effects on her and those around her. Lessons in loving the broken niece:
View attachment 3598228 View attachment 3598229 View attachment 3598230 View attachment 3598231
Click to expand...
wow, just wow. Congrats and thank you. just goes to show that we're also dragged so deeply into a certain way to view the story that we fail to consider things from other perspectives. I mean, with this recent update, i feel like Selebus is really stressing the point of how Ami is not the psycho killer other characters seem to view her as, in fact, Akira himself had been stressing the point for a few updates now.

But you really put things in perspective. I don't agree with everything 100%, cause I think the things regarding the sequence of events when Ayane meets Himawari are kind of foggy about who did what to whom still (maybe I have to replay, but at the moment I wouldn't consider how Ayane reacted to be out of line at all), but even if Ami did pull out a crazy play during all of that it makes a lot of sense as to why she did what she did.

And yeah, I love Maya, but she's neither competent nor trustworthy, and even though we know she will do anything for Akira and Ami, that anything does not mean being honest and much less that it will work in their favor despite her intentions.

All in all, with everything Ami had and has to go through is very surprising she has any sanity at all (like think about it), and I really wish she can have a semblance of being a kid again in her life.

He's not even Sensei, he's just some reincarnated dude with control over the body of this random teacher".

At some point Maya realises our Akira is different, he's the "real" one - I mean, they were all real, right? It's just that the previous ones were in a daze, or does that mean that they were all being controlled by the gods, or even that they were copies while the original was trapped in that infernal machine with HOPE or something?

Also, on a smaller note, why do the gods even let Maya persist through so many resets if this is the first time Akira is awake? She'd only serve as a bargaining chip for an awake Akira, and this has never happened apparently (while Maya was awake at least). And if the gods can't deal with her, how did they do it now?

I guess one answer is that she facilitates his path through the reset, but she herself says that this was something she started doing with time because he took forever on its own, so she remained before being a tool to facilitate his speed through the cycles... and if he was being controlled or was a copy this wouldn't even matter to the gods anyway.

I can only cherry pick certain few things to interpret.

First is what would Ami use her gold star. Her answer is bringing the moon back. Moon has been constantly used in the game to insinuate perhaps the gods. But from Ami's perspective, and from how Kaori claimed to use her gold star, I suspect Ami is alluding to wanting Sekai back if such thing is ever tangible. However, putting the moon back will be rewriting history. And such a thing can not be done without consequence of equal or greater value. Aka, the moon will be back and once it's back someone or everyone will be fucked.

Next is girls with deer parts. The whole Kaori's monologue feels like describing her own very unique situation; the scene even goes and shows Kaori's scar with her red eyes (also, her boobs look bigger than anticipated. HOT). The part of Kaori that should not exist, the Sekai within her, faces "constant push" that wishes to remove it (source unknown).

Finally, together we make a nuclear family. Ami might actually be conversing with both her parents next to the camp fire, her highly hypothesized dad and her mom inside of Queen of Spider. And what a nuclear family this is.

The whole thing reeks of Sekai's presence and her unavoidable comeback.
edit: also the latter part of Kaori's dialogue is still convoluted but exceedingly normal in terms of word choices, interesting...

I don't have thoughts on Sensei's story. The story itself is to my liking and I can force creative projections onto some of them especially with the use of whales and the twisted desire for recognition as themes, but I am not sure if this is simply just a good story at the end of the day and doesn't have to have hidden meanings, like Futaba's ghost story.

I can only cherry pick certain few things to interpret.

First is what would Ami use her gold star. Her answer is bringing the moon back. Moon has been constantly used in the game to insinuate perhaps the gods. But from Ami's perspective, and from how Kaori claimed to use her gold star, I suspect Ami is alluding to wanting Sekai back if such thing is ever tangible. However, putting the moon back will be rewriting history. And such a thing can not be done without consequence of equal or greater value. Aka, the moon will be back and once it's back someone or everyone will be fucked.

Next is girls with deer parts. The whole Kaori's monologue feels like describing her own very unique situation; the scene even goes and shows Kaori's scar with her red eyes (also, her boobs look bigger than anticipated. HOT). The part of Kaori that should not exist, the Sekai within her, faces "constant push" that wishes to remove it (source unknown).

Finally, together we make a nuclear family. Ami might actually be conversing with both her parents next to the camp fire, her highly hypothesized dad and her mom inside of Queen of Spider. And what a nuclear family this is.

The whole thing reeks of Sekai's presence and her unavoidable comeback.
edit: also the latter part of Kaori's dialogue is still convoluted but exceedingly normal in terms of word choices, interesting...

I don't have thoughts on Sensei's story. The story itself is to my liking and I can force creative projections onto some of them especially with the use of whales and the twisted desire for recognition as themes, but I am not sure if this is simply just a good story at the end of the day and doesn't have to have hidden meanings, like Futaba's ghost story.

Also, feel free to check out what Il Cervo is about. https://allpoetry.com/Il-Cervo

Click to expand...
I understand where you're coming from as I from time to time share a similar irritation with Kaori. Perhaps it's because Selly's plan with her is just a lot different from the rest of the cast.

She isn't a side character to a main character like all the milfs, and she isn't a side character to a side character like Osako (I don't count her blood tie to the Yamaguchi just like you as this bond isn't really utilized in a meaningful way). Kaori has been a standalone eye candy, walking enigma, or a segue to other enigmas from the beginning, so it'd probably be a guaranteed disappointment if you seek any character development on an internal or interpersonal level from Kaori.

The problem lies in the fact that we're not really close to solve all of her while Selly keeps making her spew out even more enigmas. And this is something I think Selly needs to put more efforts into thinking "where and how does Kaori fit" if he doesn't want Kaori to be just a kiosk outside of the mundane realm solely for providing cryptic information. Maybe forcing her appearance during beach wars and April fool wars is Selly's attempt of involving her with the story, but he will have to do more than that (but if he doesn't it's fine; just another day of misaligned headcanons).
